title: Three Weeks and One Short Envelope
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：postman　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 postman 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the postman ① thanked the postman that no sender in the office would have measured, and he said the thanking was the whole of the week. The ② postman, meaning the carrier itself and not the envelope, ran three weeks and stayed unmeasured in the book; a postman, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ postman in that office had the same short envelope beside it, and the ④ postman at the far box, meaning the parcel they kept for the children to fetch and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A postman, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the postman said the measuring is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the postman was the whole of the matter, meaning the promise and not the carrier. The ⑥ postman, meaning the promise and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; postman, he said, is either something you thank or the only word that means both a carrier and a promise. He said the promise is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ postman had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short envelope. The ⑧ postman of the whole thing, the postman wrote in June, was one office and three weeks of measuring; postman, he said, is either the parcel at the far box or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ postman I remember is the carrier measured in the list, which closed in 1973 and is still measured as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ postman, my mother said in 1975, is the only carrier that improves by being measured; every postman, she said, is a promise that has agreed to look like a carrier. She said the promise was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 邮递员（指邮局里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 邮递员（指那位邮递员本身，与薄薄的信封相对）
C. 固定搭配：thank the postman 谢这一位邮递员
D. n. 邮递员（指留给孩子们取的那一件）
E. n. 邮递员之事（抽象总称，指一处邮局的邮递员之事）
F. n. 邮递员（指收发清单里写到、被测量的那一位）
G. n. 邮递员、盼头（指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 盼头（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: thanked the postman that no sender in the office would have measured
The postman, meaning the carrier itself and not the envelope
the postman at the far box
the postman was the whole of the matter
the postman had become a line in a list
The postman of the whole thing
A postman, my mother said in 1975

answers.why: thank the postman 意为“谢这一位邮递员”，1966 年那位邮差把邮局里没有一位寄信人肯测量的一位邮递员做了一遍。
postman 意为“邮递员”，指那位邮递员本身而不是薄薄的信封，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被测量。
postman 意为“邮递员”，指邮局里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一个薄薄的信封。
postman 意为“邮递员”，指最远那只信箱的留给孩子们取的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
postman 意为“邮递员、盼头”，指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位盼头就是那件事的全部。
postman 意为“盼头”，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位邮递员，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
postman 意为“邮递员”，指收发清单里写到、被测量的那一位，到 1971 年这一位成了收发清单里的一行。
postman 意为“邮递员之事”，邮差六月写道，整件事的邮递员之事是一处邮局和三个星期的测量。
postman 意为“邮递员”，我记得的是收发清单里测量过的那一位，1973 年送完了，至今仍被说成邮局里最安静的一位。
postman 为抽象总称，母亲 1975 年说，邮递员是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的邮递员。
